utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Court is in session. Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-04-82-A, the Prosecutor versus Ljube Boskoski and Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Tarculovski, can you hear and follow the proceedings in a language you understand? THE APPELLANT TARCULOVSKI: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Can I now have the appearances starting with the representatives of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. SHIHATA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Nadia Shihata and I'm appearing on behalf of the Prosecution today with Appeals Counsel Elena Martin Salgado and Case Manager Lourdes Galicia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me now turn to the Defence counsel for Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Defence of Mr. Boskoski, Guenael Mettraux and Edina Residovic as counsel, and Jesenka Residovic, our legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Dershowitz, you are now following the proceedings via teleconference, can you hear us well? Can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the technicians help us? Is there something to be done to sort this out? Otherwise, we will proceed without having Mr. Dershowitz's participation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes? MR. A. DERSHOWITZ: [Via teleconference] Hello?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Dershowitz. Are you able to -- MR. A. DERSHOWITZ: [Via teleconference] Hi, this is Alan Dershowitz. I am hearing a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dershowitz, you are now following today's proceedings via teleconference. Can you hear us well? I repeat, Mr. Dershowitz, you are now following the proceedings via teleconference. Can you hear us? MR. A. DERSHOWITZ: [Via teleconference] Hello, this is Alan Dershowitz. I am hearing -- hello, this is Alan Dershowitz. I am listening but only in a language that I cannot understand. I am not hearing a translation into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It might be necessary to make a five-minute break so that the technicians can check everything and solve the problem. MR. A. DERSHOWITZ: [Via teleconference] I can hear you now in English. Hello? --- Break taken at 2.36 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Alan Dershowitz. MR. A. DERSHOWITZ: [Via teleconference] Alan Dershowitz is listening. I'm here on behalf of Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Pursuant to Rule 65 bis (C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal, Mr. Tarculovski, on the 29th of June, 2009, filed his written consent that a Status Conference may be conducted with his two counsel, Alan and Nathan Dershowitz, via teleconference, and I note today that Mr. Alan Dershowitz is alone today to represent Mr. Tarculovski. MR. A. DERSHOWITZ: [Via teleconference] Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This Status Conference has been convened pursuant to Rule 65 bis (B) and (C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence which provides that a Status Conference is convened within 120 days of the filing of a Notice of Appeal and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference. The main purpose of a Status Conference is to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. We last convened on the 18th of March, 2009. I recall that the Trial Chamber rendered its trial Judgement in this case on the 10th of July, 2008. I also recall that the Office of the Prosecutor filed their Notice of Appeal on the 6th of August, 2008, and that the Defence of Mr. Tarculovski filed his Notice of Appeal on the 8th of August, 2008. I now wish to address the conditions of detention and the health of Mr. Tarculovski. Mr. Tarculovski, do you have any concerns regarding your detention or your health? You have the floor. THE APPELLANT TARCULOVSKI: [Interpretation] I have no complaints, Your Honour. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You may be seated. Thank you. I am now going to turn to the scheduling matters regarding the filing of appeals briefs since our last Status Conference. Mr. Tarculovski's Defence counsel filed his notice -- his amended Notice of Appeal on the 2nd of April, 2009. The OTP filed its confidential brief, its response brief to the appeals brief on the 9th of April, 2009, and a redacted version thereof of the 16th of April, 2009. Mr. Tarculovski's Defence filed his reply brief on the 24th of April, 2009, and a redacted version thereof on the 28th of April, 2009. The Appeals Chamber is currently seized of a motion, a pending motion, filed by Mr. Tarculovski's Defence for provisional release filed on the 10th of July, 2009. The Office of the Prosecutor filed its response on the 14th of July, 2009. As to the Defence, they filed their reply on the 15th of July, 2009. Let me point out to the parties that this motion is not going to be addressed in today's hearing. The Appeals Chamber will hand down its decision as early as possible. I observe that all of the briefs have been filed. The parties will be informed in due time of a date for the appeals hearing. But I'd like to ask the parties if they have any questions they would like to address during this Status Conference at this stage of the proceedings. Let me first turn towards the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SHIHATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only issue we would raise is with respect to the date of the appeals hearing. We would greatly appreciate it if we could be given six weeks' advance notice if at all possible for planning purposes. In addition, as far as dates we might prefer, a date in early October, late November, or early December would be most helpful to us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Do Mr. Tarculovski's Defence counsel have any questions? MR. A. DERSHOWITZ: [Via teleconference] We agree that if we could receive six weeks' notice to prepare for this complicated oral argument, we would very much appreciate that as well. As I have previously informed the Court, I am a full-time professor at Harvard Law School. I teach a large class of first-year students, and I teach on Monday and Tuesday of every week, and so with the consent of the Prosecution and the agreement of the Court we would very much prefer if it's possible to have oral argument on any Thursday or Friday, that would permit me to travel to The Hague on Tuesday after my class, or Wednesday, and be available to argue on Thursday or Friday. It is possible that I could be there on time for a Wednesday argument, but that would mean that I would have to argue without any sleep, and I would, therefore, prefer if possible a Thursday and a Friday argument. The dates of early October or November or December are completely agreeable to the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Prosecutor, Mr. Dershowitz, I take due note of your observations. As I told you earlier, the date for the appeals hearing is going to be set in due time now that all the briefs have been filed. And rest assured, the observations you made will be taken on board by the Appeals Chamber when it comes to setting the date for the appeals hearing. Do you have any other questions, other questions to raise? I personally have no further points on the agenda. Therefore, I believe we can now adjourn for today. I thank the parties for their participation, and I thank the Tribunal staff for their assistance in organising this conference. The hearing stands adjourned. MR. A. DERSHOWITZ: [Via teleconference] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: at 2.49 p.m.
